Linert Contact Us Contact Advertise Submit News Statement of Values Terms of Service Public Notices Browse notices Place a notice Latest News Victims of Poland car crash, Youngstown shooting identified By Ed Runyan July 31, 2026 2 min read Trending Staff report YOUNGSTOWN -- The Mahoning County Coroner's Office has identified the child who died in a Tuesday evening crash on Route 224 in Poland and the man who was shot to death Wednesday evening on Youngstown's South Side. A Thursday press release states that the child who died was 4-year-old Cassis Huddleston, a passenger who was transferred to St. Elizabeth Youngstown Hospital after he was involved in a single vehicle accident at U.S. Route 224 and Poland Way in Poland Tuesday. An autopsy was conducted at the Cuyahoga County Medical Examiner's Office, and the incident remains under investigation by the Ohio State Highway Patrol and Mahoning County Coroner's Office. Another child was in the car who survived, as well as the driver of the car, Rosemary Huddleston, 61, who was traveling west on Route 224 when the car went off the road, struck an embankment and a tree before coming to rest in a culvert. She is from New Castle, Pa. She was transported by ambulance to St. Elizabeth Youngstown Hospital with serious injuries. A 4-month-old child was also taken there with minor injuries. SHOOTING DEATH IN YOUNGSTOWN The coroner's office also identified the man who died in a shooting in front of 2642 Glenwood Ave., Brothers Auto, on Youngstown's South Side as Kelvin Crenshaw, 20. An autopsy also was conducted at the Cuyahoga County Medical Examiner's Office in that day, and that matter remains under investigation by the Youngstown Police Department and Mahoning County Coroner's Office. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images Guinea Landslide at waste mound in Guinea capital kills 30, government says Dump site in Conakry, which minister had just promised to move, collapsed after heavy rain in west African state Reuters Sun 23 Aug 2026 18.16 EDT Last modified on Sun 23 Aug 2026 19.10 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A ⁠landslide at a huge waste dump in Guinea’s capital has killed 30 people, the government said on Sunday, after heavy rains overnight prompted it to ⁠collapse, engulfing nearby tents and shacks. The incident occurred less than a week after the government announced plans to close the ⁠site and relocate the waste because of the threat it posed, especially during the rainy season, which causes landslides and fatal flash ⁠floods each year in crowded, underdeveloped cities across parts of West Africa . The landslide took ​place at about 2am (3am UK time) ‌in the Gbessia commune ‌of Conakry, according to a government statement. The death toll was 30, with six ‌people seriously injured and 16 more lightly injured, the statement said. Rescue workers were using excavators and other tools to clear the site of the landslide, which witnesses said was large enough to bury an apartment building along with more precarious dwellings. One woman, Cire Diallo, told reporters at the scene that her five children were killed. “I ‌have lost all my children. All I can do is put my trust in God,” she said. Guinea holds the world’s largest bauxite ​reserves and richest untapped iron ore deposit at Simandou, where a massive mining project was launched in November. But the west African country has poor infrastructure and widespread poverty, with 3.7 million of its 15.1 million people living on less than $4.20 a day, according to a ⁠World Bank report published in April. On Thursday Guinea’s minister of territorial administration, Djénabou Touré Camara​, announced ​that the government was closing ​the landfill because it was unsafe and said the waste was to ​be relocated outside Conakry. The prime ‌minister, Amadou Oury ​Bah, visited ​the landfill on Sunday to assess the damage and supervise the response, the government statement said, adding that people should “remain calm, show solidarity, and strictly follow the instructions of rescue services and the competent authorities”. https://www.belfastlive.co.uk/news/man-s.text: A man has been jailed for stealing more than 50 items of post in a raid on a Belfast apartment complex. George Raducanu, 45, targeted the Arc resident development in the city’s Titanic Quarter two days after he travelled to Northern Ireland in breach of a previous deportation order. He received a four-month sentence and is set to be returned to Romania on completing the term. Raducanu, whose address was given as Link Street in Kirkcaldy, Scotland, admitted charges of burglary and illegal entry to the UK. Belfast Magistrates' Court heard a police patrol observed him in a lobby area of the apartments at Queen’s Road on August 12 this year. Officers watched as he put envelopes into a black rucksack. When Raducanu spotted police he initially struggled to find the exit button before getting out of the building. He set the bag on the ground and walked away from the scene, but was arrested in a nearby street. A prosecution lawyer said checks of the rucksack recovered 52 unopened envelopes addressed to a number of residents at the Arc complex. A pair of scissors was also located beside the bag. As Raducanu pleaded guilty to the offences today he told the court: “I’m sorry for what I did.” Defence solicitor Paul McCrudden said his client had little memory of the incident but admitted taking important items of mail once he was shown CCTV footage. “He arrived here two days before this incident,” Mr McCrudden disclosed. “Things didn’t start well and they went from bad to worse when he woke up in Musgrave PSNI station” The solicitor added that Raducanu’s wife has struggled alone in their native country to deal with family responsibilities during his absence. “Deportation proceedings have already been initiated, as soon as this case is concluded he will be returned to Romania,” Mr McCrudden confirmed. Based on Raducanu’s admissions, District Judge George Conner imposed a total sentence of four months in custody.
